title: Making People Glad to Do What You Want
coreMove: Reframe your request so the other person sees what they personally gain by saying yes, then ask in those terms

exampleSpecs.domain: a school principal asking a beloved fourth-grade teacher to give up her classroom and move to a smaller room down the hall
exampleSpecs.audience: a public-school principal handling a midyear room reshuffle
exampleSpecs.stakes: keeping the teacher's morale intact while making space for a new specialist program parents have been demanding
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the principal opens by naming, in the teacher's own language, why the new room actually suits the teacher's pride in her work, and the teacher volunteers for the move before being asked

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice nurse persuading a stubborn 82-year-old patient to start using a walker he refuses to touch
exampleSpecs.audience: a hospice nurse on a home visit
exampleSpecs.stakes: the patient's next fall will likely break a hip and end his ability to live at home, which is the one thing he says he wants
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse stops listing safety reasons and instead frames the walker as the tool that lets him keep walking his dog to the mailbox alone, and he reaches for it himself

exampleSpecs.domain: a small-town hardware store owner asking his weekend stock clerk to come in early on Black Friday
exampleSpecs.audience: the owner of a family hardware store
exampleSpecs.stakes: a no costs him the busiest morning of the year; a heavy-handed ask costs him a clerk who has other job offers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner names a specific thing the clerk has said he wants — Saturday afternoons free to coach his sister's soccer team — and shapes the early shift as the trade that protects it

exampleSpecs.domain: a divorced father asking his thirteen-year-old daughter to spend Sunday afternoons doing homework at his apartment instead of her mother's
exampleSpecs.audience: a divorced father navigating shared custody
exampleSpecs.stakes: if he pushes, she resents him; if he gives up, her grades keep slipping and her mother blames him for it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the father stops citing the custody schedule and instead points to the daughter's stated wish to make the high-school orchestra audition, framing his quieter apartment as the place that gets her there

exampleSpecs.domain: a city bus dispatcher asking a senior driver to take on a new route nobody wants, through a neighborhood with chronic schedule problems
exampleSpecs.audience: a transit dispatcher with thirty years on the job
exampleSpecs.stakes: if the senior driver refuses, the route falls to a rookie who will likely quit within a month, and the dispatcher loses a route and a driver
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the dispatcher reflects on a previous time he ordered the assignment and lost the driver, then describes the conversation where he instead named the senior driver's reputation for fixing broken routes and got a yes within two minutes

exampleSpecs.domain: a wedding caterer asking a head chef to switch from her preferred plated entrée to a family-style service the bride suddenly wants three weeks out
exampleSpecs.audience: a wedding caterer running a four-person kitchen
exampleSpecs.stakes: the chef has artistic pride in the plated dish and may walk; the wedding pays a quarter of the year's revenue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the caterer asks the chef what she would most want a guest to remember about the meal, and shapes the family-style switch as the format that delivers exactly that, so the chef proposes the change herself
